output.review_comment:
The period fix (round the division up so every started 30-day period counts) and the rounding fix (`(n + 5000) // 10000`, exact halves round up) are correct. They match the documented spec and fix real bugs.

But the PR also swaps the cap and the minimum and rewrites the docstring to match. The original docstring was explicit: "The cap always wins, even when it brings the fee below the minimum fee." The original code followed it (apply the minimum, then the cap). With this PR, a 2,000-cent balance that's 11 days late is charged 500 cents instead of the 400-cent cap, which breaks the one-fifth cap finance agreed to. The PR description doesn't say why this change was needed. The two real bugs could explain every failing test on their own.

If a test really does need the minimum to beat the cap, that's a conflict between the test and the finance docstring. It should go back to the teammate or finance, not be settled by quietly rewriting the documented spec.

Please put back the original order (minimum, then cap) and the original docstring, keep the period and rounding fixes, and run the tests again. If a test still fails only because of the order, report which test and what it expects.
